note: Discovery only. One repo per specialist means there is nowhere else to see what exists before installing it. This file is a hand-maintained list, not a registry: nothing resolves it at runtime, and installing is still `git clone` then `team-up specialist install <path>`. Fields mirror each bundle's specialist.json at the version named here — if they disagree, the bundle wins.

specialists.name: Codey
specialists.summary: Implements one ticket against a spec, with the tests that cover it.
needs: a `.team-up/commands.json` in every project it works in, defining `project-test`
its own full clone per ticket — a worktree leaves .git pointing outside the tree
specialists.caveat: Its `Write` is unbounded. Write scope is not enforceable through a tool path specifier (measured, claude 2.1.250), so what keeps it in its ticket is the disposable clone and the prompt, not a fence. Runs Opus at medium effort deliberately: never Sonnet for coding work, and effort is the cheaper lever to turn down than the model.

specialists.name: Revan
specialists.summary: Two-axis review of a merged diff: repository standards, and the originating spec.
specialists.caveat: Deliberately has no `delegate` call type: its default is `writes: "delegated_only"`, which a reviewer should not hold. Runs once, on the merged result.

specialists.name: Tessa
specialists.summary: Test strategy, regression testing, and verification that a fix does what it claims.
needs: a `.team-up/commands.json` in every project it works in, defining `project-test`

specialists.name: Reanna
specialists.summary: Source discovery and evidence synthesis, with provenance and stated uncertainty. Also scouts capabilities for other specialists.
needs: the `research.browser` or `research.context7` capability for anything a plain fetch cannot read
specialists.caveat: The only starter with network access. Its GitHub remote was renamed from team-up-with-hugo; the old URL still redirects.

capabilities.summary: Library documentation lookup: resolve a package name to a library id, then query its current docs. NOT USABLE as shipped — its descriptor runs the server through npx, which the capsule refuses.
The laziest-solution-that-works ladder, for a specialist that writes code. Costs about 1,696 description tokens.
The same ladder as a review lens. Costs about 1,094 description tokens.
Terse prose style. Chat output only — never applied to code, commits, or written files.
